title: Underived exchange along an etale morphism is the restriction identification
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $j:V\to Y$ an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $X_V=X\times_YV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $j_X:X_V\to X$ (etale, as a base change of $j$) and $f_V:X_V\to V$, and let $\square_j=(f,f_V,j,j_X)$ be the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with identification the identity of $X\times_YV$. Use the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the abelian sheaves on them [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the direct images $(u_*F)(W)=F(W\times_TU)$ for $u:U\to T$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and the inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For an abelian sheaf $G$ on $Y_{\Et}$ write $G|_V(W)=G(W\xrightarrow{p}V\xrightarrow{j}Y)$ ($p:W\to V$ etale) and $\rho_{j,G}:j^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_V$ for the natural isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]; likewise $F|_{X_V}(T)=F(T\to X_V\xrightarrow{j_X}X)$ and $\rho_{j_X,F}:j_X^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_{X_V}$ for an abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$. For an object $p:W\to V$ of $V_{\Et}$ let
$$c_W:W\times_VX_V\longrightarrow W\times_YX,\qquad c_W=(\mathrm{pr}_W,\ j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}),$$
an isomorphism of schemes over $X$ (inverse $(\mathrm{pr}_W,(\mathrm{pr}_X,p\circ\mathrm{pr}_W))$), hence an isomorphism in $X_{\Et}$, and put
$$\psi_{F,W}=F(c_W):(f_*F)|_V(W)=F(W\times_YX)\longrightarrow F(W\times_VX_V\to X)=F|_{X_V}(W\times_VX_V)=\bigl(f_{V*}(F|_{X_V})\bigr)(W).$$
Then:
1. $\psi_F=(\psi_{F,W})_W:(f_*F)|_V\to f_{V*}(F|_{X_V})$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves on $V_{\Et}$ (compatible with the restriction maps along morphisms $W'\to W$ of $V_{\Et}$), natural in $F$.
2. The underived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] $\Ex^0_{\square_j,F}:j^{-1}f_*F\to f_{V*}j_X^{-1}F$ satisfies
$$f_{V*}(\rho_{j_X,F})\circ\Ex^0_{\square_j,F}=\psi_F\circ\rho_{j,f_*F}.$$
In particular $\Ex^0_{\square_j,F}$ is an isomorphism for every abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$: the underived exchange along an etale base change is, on sections, the identity $F(W\times_YX)=F(W\times_VX_V)$.

source.place: Sites, Lemma label lemma-localize-morphism, Tag 03CF (last assertion $f'_*j_U^{-1}=j_V^{-1}f_*$) and Lemma label lemma-localize-morphism-strong, Tag 03EF; used as an identification of base change maps in Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma label lemma-base-change-local, Tag 0EZR, part (1) (literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex), and as 'it is clear that $(f_*\mathcal F)|_{\mathcal D/V}=g_*(\mathcal F|_{\mathcal C/U})$' in Cohomology on Sites, proof of Lemma Tag 0D6G (literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex); the base change map is Cohomology on Sites, Remark Tag 07A7

proof.text: *Step 1 (the objects and the isomorphisms $c_W$).* Put $h=f\circ j_X=j\circ f_V:X_V\to Y$. Let $p:W\to V$ be an object of $V_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1), applied to $f_V:X_V\to V$ and to $f:X\to Y$ with the object $j\circ p:W\to Y$ of $Y_{\Et}$ (a composite of etale morphisms, as in clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]), $\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}:W\times_VX_V\to X_V$ is an object of $(X_V)_{\Et}$ and $\mathrm{pr}_X:W\times_YX\to X$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$; $W\times_VX_V$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$ through $j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}$ (the functor $\iota_{j_X}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]). The map $c_W=(\mathrm{pr}_W,j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V})$ is defined [def-pc-fibre-product], since $j\circ p\circ\mathrm{pr}_W=j\circ f_V\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}=f\circ j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}$, and it is a morphism over $X$: $\mathrm{pr}_X\circ c_W=j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}$. It is an isomorphism: apply [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] to the diagram with rows $W\times_VX_V\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_W}W$, $X_V\xrightarrow{f_V}V$, $X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ and columns $\mathrm{pr}_{X_V},j_X$ on the left and $p,j$ on the right: the lower square $(X_V,f_V,j_X)$ is a fibre product of $j$ and $f$, the upper square is the fibre product $W\times_VX_V$ of $p$ and $f_V$, so the outer rectangle $(W\times_VX_V,\mathrm{pr}_W,j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V})$ is a fibre product of $j\circ p$ and $f$; $c_W$ is the comparison map from it to the chosen fibre product $W\times_YX$, hence an isomorphism, with inverse $(\mathrm{pr}_W,(\mathrm{pr}_X,p\circ\mathrm{pr}_W))$ (both composites are the identity by the uniqueness in the universal properties). Its inverse is again over $X$, so $c_W$ is an isomorphism in $X_{\Et}$. More generally, for a morphism $a:W'\to W$ of $V_{\Et}$, the two morphisms $c_W\circ(a\times_V\mathrm{id}_{X_V})$ and $(a\times_Y\mathrm{id}_X)\circ c_{W'}:W'\times_VX_V\to W\times_YX$ have the same components $a\circ\mathrm{pr}_{W'}$ and $j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}$, hence are equal [def-pc-fibre-product]. (In Stacks 03CF this is the equality $u'(V')=u(V')$ of the localized functor: $V'\times_YX$ seen over $X\times_YV$.)

source.place: Sites, Lemma label lemma-localize-morphism (Tag 03CF), proof: $(j_V^{-1}f_*\mathcal F)(V'/V)=f_*\mathcal F(V')=\mathcal F(u(V'))=(j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)(u(V')/U)=(f'_*j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)(V'/V)$; Lemma label lemma-localize-morphism-strong (Tag 03EF)

proof.text: *Step 2 (sections of the two sheaves).* By clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (for $j$ and for $j_X$), $(f_*F)|_V$ and $F|_{X_V}$ are abelian sheaves, and by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] so is $f_{V*}(F|_{X_V})$. On an object $p:W\to V$ of $V_{\Et}$: $(f_*F)|_V(W)=(f_*F)(W\xrightarrow{j p}Y)=F(W\times_YX)$, and $f_{V*}(F|_{X_V})(W)=F|_{X_V}(W\times_VX_V)=F(W\times_VX_V\xrightarrow{j_X\mathrm{pr}}X)$; on a morphism $a:W'\to W$ of $V_{\Et}$ the restriction maps are $F(a\times_Y\mathrm{id}_X)$ and $F(a\times_V\mathrm{id}_{X_V})$ respectively (the direct image acts on morphisms by base change, and $G|_V$, $F|_{X_V}$ have the restriction maps of $G$, $F$). These are the two outer terms of the chain of equalities in the proof of Stacks 03CF.

source.place: Sites, Lemma label lemma-localize-morphism (Tag 03CF), proof: $(j_V^{-1}f_*\mathcal F)(V'/V)=f_*\mathcal F(V')=\mathcal F(u(V'))=(j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)(u(V')/U)=(f'_*j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)(V'/V)$; Lemma label lemma-localize-morphism-strong (Tag 03EF)

proof.text: *Step 3 (clause 1: $\psi_F$ is a natural isomorphism of sheaves).* By step 1, $c_W$ is an isomorphism of $X_{\Et}$, so $\psi_{F,W}=F(c_W)$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups with inverse $F(c_W^{-1})$. For $a:W'\to W$ in $V_{\Et}$, applying the contravariant functor $F$ to the equality $c_W\circ(a\times_V\mathrm{id}_{X_V})=(a\times_Y\mathrm{id}_X)\circ c_{W'}$ of step 1 gives $F(a\times_V\mathrm{id}_{X_V})\circ\psi_{F,W}=\psi_{F,W'}\circ F(a\times_Y\mathrm{id}_X)$, i.e. by step 2 $\psi_F$ commutes with the restriction maps; so $\psi_F$ is a morphism of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] (a morphism of the underlying presheaves) and, its components being bijective, an isomorphism (the components $F(c_W^{-1})$ form the inverse morphism). Naturality in $F$: for a morphism $\varphi:F\to F'$ the morphisms $(f_*\varphi)|_V$ and $f_{V*}(\varphi|_{X_V})$ have components $\varphi(W\times_YX)$ and $\varphi(W\times_VX_V)$ (step 2), and $\varphi(W\times_VX_V)\circ F(c_W)=F'(c_W)\circ\varphi(W\times_YX)$ is the naturality of $\varphi$ along $c_W$. This is clause 1, the isomorphism $f'_*j_U^{-1}=j_V^{-1}f_*$ of Stacks 03CF for the localization of the morphism of sites $f$ at $V$ (Stacks 03EF identifies the localized morphism with $f_V$).

source.place: Sites, Lemma label lemma-localize-morphism (Tag 03CF), proof: $(j_V^{-1}f_*\mathcal F)(V'/V)=f_*\mathcal F(V')=\mathcal F(u(V'))=(j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)(u(V')/U)=(f'_*j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)(V'/V)$; Lemma label lemma-localize-morphism-strong (Tag 03EF)

proof.text:
*Step 4 (reduction to the transposes under $j^{-1}\dashv j_*$).* Write $A=f_*F$ and $B=F|_{X_V}$. Both sides of the equality of clause 2 are morphisms $j^{-1}A\to f_{V*}B$. By [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], $j^{-1}$ is left adjoint to $j_*$ with unit $\eta_j$, so $\alpha\mapsto j_*(\alpha)\circ\eta_{j,A}$ is a bijection from morphisms $j^{-1}A\to f_{V*}B$ to morphisms $A\to j_*f_{V*}B$. Hence it suffices to show $L=R$ for
$$L=j_*\bigl(f_{V*}(\rho_{j_X,F})\circ\Ex^0_{\square_j,F}\bigr)\circ\eta_{j,A},\qquad R=j_*(\psi_F\circ\rho_{j,A})\circ\eta_{j,A},$$
and, these being morphisms of sheaves on $Y_{\Et}$, it suffices to compare their components at every object $t:T\to Y$ of $Y_{\Et}$. Write $T_V=T\times_YV$ (an object of $V_{\Et}$ via $\mathrm{pr}_V$), $p_T:T_V\to T$ the projection, and $T_X=T\times_YX$.

source.place: written by the agent: the comparison with the exchange morphism is not in Stacks (asserted without argument in Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma Tag 0EZR (1), literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex); it follows the mate argument of the source Lean AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.baseChangeMap_flip_eq (WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/BaseChange/Etale.lean, branch slopmaster2)

proof.text:
*Step 5 (the right side on sections).* By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $j_*(\beta)(T)=\beta(T_V)$ for a morphism $\beta$ of sheaves on $V_{\Et}$. By clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] for the etale $j$ and $G=A$, $\rho_{j,A}(T_V)\circ\eta_{j,A}(T)=A(p_T)$, the restriction of $A=f_*F$ along $p_T$, which by step 2 is $F(p_T\times_Y\mathrm{id}_X):F(T_X)\to F(T_V\times_YX)$. Then $\psi_F(T_V)=F(c_{T_V})$. Hence
$$R(T)=F(c_{T_V})\circ F(p_T\times_Y\mathrm{id}_X)=F(m_T),\qquad m_T=(p_T\times_Y\mathrm{id}_X)\circ c_{T_V}:T_V\times_VX_V\to T_X,$$
and by the definition of $c_{T_V}$ (step 1) the components of $m_T$ are $\mathrm{pr}_T\circ\mathrm{pr}_{T_V}$ (to $T$) and $j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}$ (to $X$).

proof.text:
*Step 6 (the left side through the composition isomorphisms).* By [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], $\Ex^0_{\square_j,F}$ is the adjoint under $f_V^{-1}\dashv f_{V*}$ of $j_X^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,F}\circ\theta_{\square_j,A}$, i.e. $\Ex^0_{\square_j,F}=f_{V*}(j_X^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,F}\circ\theta_{\square_j,A})\circ\eta_{f_V,j^{-1}A}$. The specified isomorphism of the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] is the composite of composition isomorphisms $\theta_{\square_j}=c_{f,j_X}^{-1}\circ c_{j,f_V}:f_V^{-1}j^{-1}\to h^{-1}\to j_X^{-1}f^{-1}$, with $c_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\to(u\circ v)^{-1}$ and $d_{u,v}:(u\circ v)_*\to u_*v_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (this is the definition of the attached source Lean `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.squareUpperStarIso`: `(upperStarComp f' g (g' ≫ f) sq.w).symm ≪≫ upperStarComp g' f`); both composites $j\circ f_V$ and $f\circ j_X$ are the one morphism $h$. (a) Clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] for $(u,v)=(j,f_V)$ and $G=A$ gives $j_*f_{V*}(c_{j,f_V,A})\circ j_*(\eta_{f_V,j^{-1}A})\circ\eta_{j,A}=d_{j,f_V,h^{-1}A}\circ\eta_{h,A}$; with the naturality of $d_{j,f_V}$ (clause 1) this gives
$$j_*(\Ex^0_{\square_j,F})\circ\eta_{j,A}=d_{j,f_V,j_X^{-1}F}\circ h_*(j_X^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,F})\circ h_*(c_{f,j_X,A}^{-1})\circ\eta_{h,A}.$$
(b) Clause 2 for $(u,v)=(f,j_X)$ and $G=A$ gives $\eta_{h,A}=d_{f,j_X,h^{-1}A}^{-1}\circ f_*j_{X*}(c_{f,j_X,A})\circ f_*(\eta_{j_X,f^{-1}A})\circ\eta_{f,A}$; by the naturality of $d_{f,j_X}$, $h_*(c^{-1}_{f,j_X,A})\circ d^{-1}_{f,j_X,h^{-1}A}=d^{-1}_{f,j_X,j_X^{-1}f^{-1}A}\circ f_*j_{X*}(c^{-1}_{f,j_X,A})$, so $h_*(c^{-1}_{f,j_X,A})\circ\eta_{h,A}=d^{-1}_{f,j_X,j_X^{-1}f^{-1}A}\circ f_*(\eta_{j_X,f^{-1}A})\circ\eta_{f,A}$. (c) By the naturality of $d_{f,j_X}$, of $\eta_{j_X}$ (along $\varepsilon_{f,F}:f^{-1}A\to F$) and the triangle identity $f_*(\varepsilon_{f,F})\circ\eta_{f,f_*F}=\mathrm{id}_{f_*F}$ of $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]: $h_*(j_X^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,F})\circ d^{-1}_{f,j_X,j_X^{-1}f^{-1}A}\circ f_*(\eta_{j_X,f^{-1}A})\circ\eta_{f,A}=d^{-1}_{f,j_X,j_X^{-1}F}\circ f_*(\eta_{j_X,F})\circ f_*(\varepsilon_{f,F})\circ\eta_{f,A}=d^{-1}_{f,j_X,j_X^{-1}F}\circ f_*(\eta_{j_X,F})$. Together:
$$j_*(\Ex^0_{\square_j,F})\circ\eta_{j,A}=d_{j,f_V,j_X^{-1}F}\circ d^{-1}_{f,j_X,j_X^{-1}F}\circ f_*(\eta_{j_X,F})$$
(the exchange morphism is the mate of the composition isomorphism of direct images). Composing with $j_*f_{V*}(\rho_{j_X,F})$ and using the naturality of $d_{j,f_V}$ and $d_{f,j_X}$ once more:
$$L=d_{j,f_V,B}\circ d^{-1}_{f,j_X,B}\circ f_*\bigl(j_{X*}(\rho_{j_X,F})\circ\eta_{j_X,F}\bigr).$$

proof.text: *Step 7 (the left side on sections; clause 2).* Evaluate the formula of step 6 at $T$. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $f_*(\gamma)(T)=\gamma(T_X)$. By clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] for the etale $j_X$ and the object $T_X$ of $X_{\Et}$, $\rho_{j_X,F}(T_X\times_XX_V)\circ\eta_{j_X,F}(T_X)=F(q)$, $q:T_X\times_XX_V\to T_X$ the projection. By clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], $d_{f,j_X,B}(T)=B(k_1)$ and $d_{j,f_V,B}(T)=B(k_2)$ for the canonical isomorphisms $k_1=(\mathrm{pr}_T\circ\mathrm{pr}_{T_X},\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}):T_X\times_XX_V\to T\times_YX_V$ and $k_2=(\mathrm{pr}_T\circ\mathrm{pr}_{T_V},\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}):T_V\times_VX_V\to T\times_YX_V$ ($T\times_YX_V$ formed with $h$) [def-pc-fibre-product]; and $B(k)=F(k)$, $B=F|_{X_V}$ having the restriction maps of $F$. So $L(T)=F(k_2)\circ F(k_1)^{-1}\circ F(q)=F(q\circ k_1^{-1}\circ k_2)$. Now $k_1^{-1}=((\mathrm{pr}_T,j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}),\mathrm{pr}_{X_V})$, so $q\circ k_1^{-1}=(\mathrm{pr}_T,j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}):T\times_YX_V\to T_X$, and $q\circ k_1^{-1}\circ k_2$ has components $\mathrm{pr}_T\circ\mathrm{pr}_{T_V}$ and $j_X\circ\mathrm{pr}_{X_V}$: it is the morphism $m_T$ of step 5, by the uniqueness in the universal property of $T_X$. Hence $L(T)=F(m_T)=R(T)$ for every $T$, so $L=R$, and by step 4 $f_{V*}(\rho_{j_X,F})\circ\Ex^0_{\square_j,F}=\psi_F\circ\rho_{j,f_*F}$: clause 2. Finally $\Ex^0_{\square_j,F}=f_{V*}(\rho_{j_X,F})^{-1}\circ\psi_F\circ\rho_{j,f_*F}$ is a composite of isomorphisms (clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], step 3, and $f_{V*}$ a functor), hence an isomorphism; on sections it is the identification $F(W\times_YX)=F(W\times_VX_V)$ through $c_W$.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against Stacks 03CF/03EF and the definitions of Ex^0, theta, rho; correct, no hypothesis on f). Proof in 7 steps, no new node. Clause 1 (steps 1-3) follows the proof of Stacks 03CF: c_W is an isomorphism over X by the pasting leaf lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting (with lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits (1) for the objects), its compatibility with restriction maps and naturality in F are elementary.
